title: Holding More Than One Healthy Options Card Programme
content:
A member may hold at most the tier's maximum number of allowance programmes at one time, so that a member on a health plan with an everyday card and a separate chronic care card is served properly rather than refused. Across every tier of the Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card that maximum stands at 2 programmes at one time.

**The duplicate test.** No other allowance programme of the same official name is already open for this member in the same benefit year. The test is made on the plan's own programme records before a programme is opened, and it is made on the member reference the new programme would be opened under: the records are read for the card's official name, the benefit year and the standing of each programme the member already holds. A programme counts as open for this test where its standing is anything other than closed — its enrollment recorded, its card issued, the card in use, the card stopped, or the card dormant. Programmes are told apart by their benefit year and by the day the programme started.

**What follows from the test.**

| What the records show | What is done |
|---|---|
| A programme of the same official name already open for this member in the same benefit year | Two programmes of the same name in one benefit year are always a duplicate, however they were raised, and the second is not opened; the member is shown the one they already hold and its balance |
| A programme of the same official name open, but for a different benefit year | Programmes in different benefit years are never duplicates |
| The member already holds the maximum of 2 programmes | A new programme is opened only after one of the existing ones is closed, and the member is told what closing it would forfeit |

A member's history ordinarily shows one closed programme for each year they have been with the plan, and that is not a sign of duplication.

**Basis Q&A.** A member holds a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card - Core programme opened this benefit year and asks for a second Core programme in the same year: the duplicate test is met against them and the second is not opened; they are shown the Core programme they hold and its balance. A member holds a Core programme for the previous benefit year, closed, and a Core programme for this one: those are programmes of different benefit years and are not duplicates.
